summary:
# NOTES: "Shadowed by a Detective; or, The Woman in Wax" (Virginia Champlin / René de Pont-Jest), Magnet Detective Library No. 106, Street & Smith

## Front matter (non-story)
- Magnet Library ad pages: list of Nos. 1–105 (e.g., No. 96 "No. 13 Rue Marlot" by Rene du Pont Jest; No. 72 Sherlock Holmes; No. 105 "A Bite of an Apple"). Street & Smith "To the Reader" blurb. Copyright 1885 J. S. Ogilvie & Co.; 1899 Street & Smith.
- Contents: Ch I The Kidnapping (p.5); II What Became of the Heroine (12); III Robertson Brothers & Co. (26); IV Honorable Willie Saunders Becomes Thoroughly Mad (43); V Shakespeare's Tavern (53); VI The Morgue at Bellevue Hospital (62); VII Saunders almost loses his Mind, while Captain Young loses his time (74); VIII Taking a Cast of the Dead (84); IX Coroner Davis / Robertson Jr. convinced (92); X A Mohick... Big Kelly... William Dow transforms a visitor into a prisoner (100); XI A Criminal Court (115); XII Mr. Midler exhorts penitents (127); XIII James Gobson escapes the Gallows; Davis' remorse (137); XIV Saunders passes from despair to amazement to anger (149); XV William Dow's Remorse (161); XVI William Dow's Revenge—seeking the unknown (169); XVII A Souvenir of Love (184); XVIII Two Villas at Jamaica Plain (196); XIX What happened on leaving Barker's (204); XX A wife's love and a maid's love (217); XXI The murderer of a Dead Woman (226); XXII Kitty Bell's Story (238); XXIII Wharf 32 (247).
- Transcriber's note: serialized in Boston Globe May 3–June 11, 1884 as "The woman of wax; or, Memoirs of a detective"; translation of *La femme de cire* (middle of William Dow trilogy).
- Ads at end (Ripans Tabules, Buckingham's Dye, Nicholas Carter list, Conan Doyle, Barclay North) — non-story.

## Characters
- **Ada Ricard** (formerly Mrs. James Gobson; real name Anna Bell): blonde, steel-blue eyes, ~25; torn left ear (diamond hides cut), missing right-side tooth (pearl lacking). Lived 17 East 23rd St, NYC. Diamond solitaire earrings (~$10,000), gifts from Saunders.
- **Kitty Bell**: twin of Anna; resembles her; took her place; sentenced 1 year; later café success in NY, then Paris.
- **Willie Saunders**: stout cracker-merchant (~50), vain, jealous, Brooklyn factories, worth ~$1.5M; Highland costume at ball; later loses mind, keeps wax statue, later sold to Barnum's Museum.
- **James Gobson**: Buffalo merchant, brutal, jealous; tore Ada's ear, knocked out tooth; went West; tall, ~40, beard no mustache. Acquitted in revision; married Ada again in Boston; killed 2nd time (dagger), shot at wax, arrested; sent to Blackwell's Island; jumped into river, body found under Wharf 32.
- **Colonel Edward Forster**: Union Army, blond, ~35, yacht *Gleam* (Captain Reynolds); hired kidnapper; promised $1,000.
- **Mary**: Ada's maid, saucy; took $100 from Saunders; later refused to ID body; hid at Washington Hotel; later absent.
- **July**: former maid who recognized torn ear.
- **Fat Kelly**: chief of metropolitan police, huge, churlish; elected/re-elected; rival of Edward Robertson (Sr.).
- **Captain Young** ("Master Young"): detective captain, giant, brave, dim; "terrible Young."
- **William Dow**: former Philadelphia doctor, retired, detective; alias "Charles Murray" in Boston; ward/charge **Miss Jane** (16, blonde, blue eyes; "my friend"); governess **Mrs. Wandright**.
- **Robertson Brothers & Co.** agency, 22 Nineteenth St.; **Robertson, Jr.** (~30, pomaded, foppish); Sr. (founded out of spite toward Kelly).
- **Coroner Davis** (Saint Vincent district); **Sheriff Mortimer**; **Dr. O'Neel** (Bellevue head surgeon, autopsy report); **Albert Moor** (modeler, made head cast and full wax body); **Lawyer Macready** (defense); **O'Brien** (State prosecutor); **Judge Douglas** (chief justice, Criminal Court); **Mr. Peters** (Tombs manager); **Meyer** (hangman, broke leg); **Rev. Mr. Midler** (Methodist, port & ham); **Robert Fowl** (former coachman, falsely IDs body); **Tom Katters** (livery driver; Thompson's stable, 4 Sixth Ave); **Toby** (watchman, Wharf 43, tar barrel); **Charley** & **Jim** (Firefly sailors); **Thomas Bright & Davidson** (Shakespeare's Tavern owners, South St, Wharf 32); **Harris Burnett** (Gobson's club friend, Kelly/Dow agent); **Charles Murray** (= Dow); **Betsy** (Ada's maid in Boston); **Captain Semmas** (Fort Dakota); **John Butler** (trapper guide); **Jimin** (Swift Deer, Sioux chief); **Washah & Winka** (Sioux warriors who were masks); **Makeni** (Winka's wife, bracelet); **Thomas Bernett** (Union Hotel porter, Jefferson City); **Tom Byng** (stage driver); **Mr. Burnett/Harris**; **Captain Reynolds**; **James Davis** (mate of steamer *Liberia*).

## Chapter-by-chapter events
**I.** Winter 1865 ball at Ada's (masquerade). Background: Ada's husband Gobson; she had Thomas Cornhill (oil wells, died), then Saunders. Forster a suitor. Three Sioux masks: tallest carries Ada out to landau; two ride box; carriage flees east along First Ave; Ada's cry unheard.
**II.** Saunders cries, Mary laughs, takes $100, says Forster likely. Landau stops; Indians vanish; carriage to Yorkville; man carries Ada to small house; then rows her in boat across East River past Blackwell's Island to Greenpoint (rower is Indian; "Colonel" appointed opposite shore). Forster's coupe at Greenpoint; Forster pays rower; carriage to Brooklyn wharf; yacht *Gleam*; Ada's blue silk robe; supper. Forster's confession: Cornhill talked of Ada; hired man proposed kidnapping.
**III.** Saunders wakes ~1pm; Ada's letter ("absent a month... Ada Ricard"); Kelly rebuffs Saunders; Robertson Jr. recruits him; agency fee $500 + $500; photo of Ada; agency report (Thompson's stable, coachman Katters, yawl seen by Liberia's mate, Gleam at Staten Island, cylinder repairs); Saunders pays $1,000 advance; sets out.
**IV.** Saunders & Robertson on steamer *Firefly* (Battery wharf); anchor near *Gleam* off Staten Island; Saunders rows in fishing boat toward villa; collision with Forster's yawl in fog; woman's cries; Saunders falls on shore; *Gleam* leaves; sailors paid $100 each for silence. Saunders summoned to Kelly; flees to Bellevue.
**V.** Shakespeare's Tavern (oyster room); Firefly sailors drink hush money; Toby, Charley; body found at Wharf 43/32 with tar barrel tied to right leg (Ch VI says "above right knee"); coroner Davis; body to morgue.
**VI.** Crowd at Bellevue; O'Neel's autopsy report (no foam, not drowned, arsenic-user, missing right second canine, scar left ear, chloroform suspected). Kelly orders Young. Fowl IDs body (missing tooth right side). Saunders faints at morgue, confesses "I killed you"; Young & Dow; Dow advises taking Saunders home.
**VII.** Kelly, Mortimer, Young search Ada's house; Mary refuses to ID body at morgue; Mary stays at Washington Hotel; servant registry system; Albert Moor engaged. Robertson visits Saunders.
**VIII.** July IDs ear. Moor makes plaster cast at night; Dow performs surgical closure; full cast later; Dow: "this woman of stone will accuse herself."
**IX.** Inquest: Toby, Thompson, Katters; $100 reward; $1,000 reward; Gobson suspected (seen at Jefferson, MO); Robertson's theory (fisherman); Moor delivers wax head; displayed in glass case.
**X.** Gobson's card; visits morgue; denies recognizing; insurance $20,000 Gresham Co.; Dow's reasoning (Indians from Sioux); Young arrests; Gobson pulls revolver; Dow shoots it from behind curtain; taken to Tombs.
**XI.** Trial at Criminal Court: O'Brien prosecutes; Macready defends; guilty verdict; death sentence; execution set on 25th (Wednesday).
**XII.** Dow's household (Miss Jane, Mrs. Wandright); Midler's visit; Gobson and Midler breakfast; Meyer's accident postpones hanging one day.
**XIII.** Inventory at Ada's house; Ada returns alive; Gobson released on $100 bail; Kelly/Davis humiliated; Ada reveals ear/tooth.
**XIV.** Crowd; Gobson and Ada on balcony; Saunders visits, rejected; Dow takes Saunders's report and photo; "I think I am beginning to understand."
**XV.** Forster questioned; revision trial; Ada speaks; Gobson acquitted; Dow promises Kelly 10,000 votes; leaves with Young.
**XVI.** Dow, Young, Saunders to Jefferson City (Union Hotel); porter/driver/barber identify Gobson (early January); Omaha; John Butler; Fort Dakota (Capt. Semmas); Sioux village of Jimin; Washah & Winka (masks); Makeni's gold bracelet (initials, date engraved).
**XVII.** Bracelet bargained; Dow reveals Ada married Gobson again; Dow goes to San Francisco; Saunders and Young to Chicago.
**XVIII.** Gobson & Ada in Boston at Jamaica Plain villa (No. 66); Charles Murray (Dow) at No. 67; Ada's love letter; Jane watches.
**XIX.** Harris Burnett (Dow's agent) feeds Gobson drinks at Barker's; cab trick (wheel nut); attack staged; Murray "saves" Gobson; champagne at villa; Gobson's hatred.
**XX.** Murray and Ada lovers; Jane faints (jealous); Murray writes letter to Kelly/Davis/Young ("The hour has come"). Saunders and Young at American House.
**XXI.** Gobson told Davis threat; Ada's letter; plan to elope; Dow's staged warning "letter found on door-step" addressed to Davis; Gobson arrives; dagger strikes wax statue; shot at wax; arrested; Saunders "Poor Ada!"
**XXII.** Kitty Bell's Story: Dow reveals wax body; baptism certificate (New Orleans, June 14, 186-, twins Kitty & Anna Bell, born 13 Feb); Gobson drugged Kitty in San Francisco, knocked out tooth, pulled ear; Gobson plotted; took her to Forster; sent "A. Z." signal; murdered Anna in carriage; Kitty played Ada.
**XXIII.** Wharf 32: Gobson jumps off Blackwell's Island, drowns; body found under Wharf 32 opposite Shakespeare's. Dow's reasoning explained to Kelly; Kelly re-elected (20,000 more votes); Kitty sentenced 1 year, released, later café and Paris; Mary not found; wax statue sold to Barnum's. Dow's secret tie to Jane; "some day we may narrate."

## Key quoted phrases
- Ada's ear: "a huge diamond"; "pearl lacking."
- Dow: "Who knows if this will not be more than a work of art, and if this woman of stone will not accuse herself some day."
- Dow: "I made him murder her a second time."
- Kelly: "Devil take William Dow."
- Gobson's last words in cell/Boston: "If I thought those men were set on by her I would kill her as I would a dog."
